clues: This town sits in a narrow river valley in the north of Turkey. It lies just inland from the Black Sea shore.
It sits high above the sea that lies close by. So it has an inland climate, not a coast one, and its air suits apple trees.
In old Ottoman times, young princes were sent here to rule. They came to learn and gain skill before they might rule the whole land.
Look up from the old wood homes by the river. High on the cliffs you can see tombs cut for kings of old.
Old Ottoman wood houses line the banks of the river. Now they serve as cafes and inns where guests can eat and rest.
